description: Backfill the three Copernicus products Open-Meteo does not redistribute -- AgERA5 agrometeorological indicators on the classic CDS host with zero new credential plumbing, CEMS fire danger indices behind a new, separately-registered EWDS host and key, and seasonal forecasts scoped as a later, lower-confidence phase -- reusing historical_era5.py's working cdsapi client, checkpointing and raw-cache shape as the integration template rather than inventing a second one
dependency_mode: Python only inside services/agri-data-service/src/agri_data_service (new HistoricalAgera5*/HistoricalCems* contract classes and execution/historical_agera5.py, execution/historical_cems.py modules, following historical_era5.py's shape -- not its literal classes, since dataset id, request cardinality and coverage rules all differ). No Alembic revision for AgERA5: agri.data_source.key is DML like every existing lane. CEMS is Python-plus-config, not Python-only -- it needs two new Settings fields (an EWDS URL and key, mirroring cdsapi_url/cdsapi_key at config.py:132-133), a second local .env entry, and a second Railway credential pair, none of which is a schema change but all of which is new plumbing this repo has never carried before. Seasonal forecasts are scoping and an open-question list only in this track; no code is authored for them. Every plan is a new plan file, a new release_set.logical_key and a new manifest_checksum, per the rule this repo already runs nine times over -- never an edit to era5-land-pnw-soil-20220430-20260430.json or its sibling, which stay retired for soil state and untouched.
activation_gate: Phase 1 (AgERA5) ships first and needs no gate beyond its own two early tasks: evaluate sis-agrometeorological-indicators-timeseries against the existing 0.1-degree cell lattice before committing to the gridded sis-agrometeorological-indicators product, and confirm live per-variable-per-statistic request cardinality on the CDS request form before any plan file is checksummed -- an unverified cardinality assumption here costs the same full re-fetch that an unverified Open-Meteo field name costs in the sibling track. It reuses the same classic cds.climate.copernicus.eu credentials the retired soil lane already has, so no credential gate applies. Phase 2 (CEMS) is explicitly gated behind provisioning a second, separately-registered Copernicus Early Warning Data Store (ewds.climate.copernicus.eu) account, its own terms click-through, and threading a new key pair through Settings/.env/Railway -- this must be surfaced and confirmed working (a successful non-404 request against cems-fire-historical-v1) before any CEMS plan is authored, precisely so the 'dataset not found' failure mode (the classic client silently pointed at the wrong host) is caught at activation time and not at retrieve() time. Phase 2 also opens with a live-request-form check of the 0.25 vs 0.5 degree grid discrepancy between the EWDS landing page and the Confluence API guide before checksumming. Phase 3 (seasonal) does not start in this track -- it is scoped and its open questions are recorded, but its dataset ids were not verified to the same standard as phases 1 and 2 and it waits on an owner decision to become its own track. Phases 1 and 2 touch disjoint files (different execution/historical_*.py modules, different plan directories) and could ship in either order once each phase's own gate clears, but AgERA5 is sequenced first because it is strictly cheaper -- no new credential surface -- and de-risks the reused-template shape before CEMS adds a second host on top of it.
